correctness.rationale: A circular cover of length L is a closed de Bruijn walk containing all binom(n,2) mandatory edges. Required edges form disjoint necklace-rotation cycles. The balanced residual edge multigraph has t=L-binomial(n,2) extra edges. For t<=n-2, all residual elementary cycles have lengths <=n-2; two distinct such cycles cannot intersect because their common (n-1)-bit vertex would have periods p,q and Fine–Wilf would make them identical. A short cycle touching the adjacent-one required component touches no other required component, since it cannot contain a singleton-one boundary vertex and periodic occurrences of 11 force all its vertices to contain 11. Thus a cover cannot connect the mandatory components with fewer than n-1 extra edges. Conversely n-2 singleton-one edges and a duplicate endpoint-ones edge form a directed connecting cycle through all singleton-one vertices, making a connected balanced graph with an Euler circuit of length binom(n,2)+n-1. Fully specified for all integers n>=4; executable standard-library verifier has checked the exact multiset of construction factors through n=15 and independent finite lower sanity checks at n=4,5.

value.rationale: This closes an original natural exact-minimum circular binary universal-covering question posed in the 2010 literature for the first nontrivial fixed weight where the required de Bruijn subgraph is disconnected. The value is the sharp all-length minimal augmentation cost, not an arbitrary one-off improvement: it requires a substantive periodicity argument to prove optimality and gives an explicit combinatorial construction. It identifies exactly which n-1 additional edges suffice and why n-2 can never suffice, yielding a reusable structural obstruction for other constrained languages.
